items_missed: Never got or used the customer's name — not once in 15.6 minutes
No agenda statement with a rough timeframe

Never captured origin or destination addresses or zips — the only location detail in the entire call is the customer volunteering 'we're still in Missouri City'. A five-mover, two-truck job was reserved on the schedule with no confirmed addresses
Never asked about stairs or floor levels at the origin (the 'one story' detail came from the customer about the new house)
Never asked about additional stops, storage stops, parking/access/HOA, walk distance, or box count
Never asked about specialty or heavy items — no piano, safe, gym equipment, or antiques question on a four-bedroom home

No Worries Damage Coverage ($2,000) never mentioned — the customer opened the call asking 'what will you all do to protect the furniture' and said 'I just wanted to kind of get that insurance from all that'. He was answered with moving blankets and floor runners and never heard about damage coverage or 60¢/lb valuation. This is the single clearest miss on the call
No 'pricing is super simple' opener and no 'no hidden fees' pitch

Clock: never said the clock starts on-site when the contract opens, never mentioned 15-minute prorated increments, no sense-check (only the 2.5-hour minimum was covered, and only because the customer asked)
Never mentioned that no deposit is required — even when the customer asked what happens next and what he'd receive
Zero Save Your Ass content, despite the customer twice trying to reduce the crew size to save money
No 'reply with any corrections', no bolded detail list at the top of the email, no hours or how to reach us

Estimate accuracy risk: the rep held the reservation at a five-mover / two-truck / 7-8 hour, ~$3,500-$4,000 quote after the customer said twice they don't have much furniture and suggested three or four movers, and openly said 'we're hopefully on the over quoting the move' rather than sizing to the described inventory or using an equivalent to justify the crew
The virtual walkthrough explanation cost several minutes of circular back-and-forth — the customer repeatedly asked whether to send videos, whether it was live, and which house it covered
top_strength: He asked for the business directly — 'do you wanna make a reservation on the schedule or did you just want to get a quote sent over now?' — and converted a quote call into a Wednesday reservation with a virtual walkthrough booked for the same day. He also captured the customer's hardwood-floor concern as a note for the crew and threw in the three mattress bags to close the objection.
coaching_note: This customer led with a damage question and never got the damage answer — run No Worries ($2,000 coverage) any time protection comes up, not just blankets and floor runners. Second: never reserve a truck and crew without capturing both addresses, and size the crew to the inventory rather than deliberately over-quoting, which is exactly the pattern driving our estimate-accuracy gap.
phone_presence_notes: Consistently polite and accommodating ('no worries', 'yes sir') and the customer closed with 'I appreciate your help', but zero name use and a mechanical, question-answer rhythm that let the customer circle the same walkthrough question three or four times without the rep resetting the explanation.
